Entity: User (single entity with role field)
nodes.rationale: One User entity with a role field instead of a separate Provider entity, so a provider can also act as a consumer and roles are a data change, not a schema change.

nodes.label: Entity: AvailabilitySlot (bound to provider, not service)
nodes.rationale: The slot belongs to the person, not the service, so booking it for one service consumes it for every other service that provider offers - this is what prevents double-booking a human.

nodes.label: Entity: GoogleAccountConnection (per-provider OAuth tokens)
nodes.rationale: Stores each provider's encrypted refresh token + googleEmail, with a nullable fallbackMeetUrl for providers who skip OAuth entirely.

nodes.label: Entity: AppSettings (single-row typed settings)
nodes.rationale: A single-row typed table was chosen over a generic key/value table and over yaml-only config, because yaml cannot be written or refreshed live in production; the default is seeded from application.yaml and cached at runtime.

nodes.label: MVP Scope (6 in-scope areas, payments/reviews out)
nodes.rationale: Bootcamp rule of 3-5 core feature areas; payments/billing, ratings/reviews and multi-tenant orgs deliberately excluded from the MVP.

nodes.label: BookIt Design System (teal tokens, core components)
nodes.rationale: Design-System-first in Claude Design (tokens + core components) so every generated screen stays consistent, then pulled into the repo one component at a time via DesignSync.

nodes.label: Availability-pressure palette (High/Medium/Low/None)
nodes.rationale: Kept visually distinct from the teal primary and reinforced with a numeric badge + opacity rather than colour alone, so it stays readable and colourblind-safe. Weekends are not special: a day is shadowed only when it has 0 available slots.

nodes.label: Max booking horizon (admin-configurable, default 6 months)
nodes.rationale: Bounds how far ahead consumers may book; enforced both in the calendar UI and in server-side booking validation so the client filter is never the only gate.

nodes.label: Provider advance limit (ceil(horizon x 1.5), derived)
nodes.rationale: Derived rather than stored (multiplier is yaml-only, not admin-facing) so providers can pre-load availability further ahead than consumers can currently book; the rolling window makes those slots bookable as time advances.

nodes.label: Key rule: booking a slot reserves it across the provider's services
nodes.rationale: Because the slot belongs to the person and not to a service, one booking consumes that time for every service that provider offers - the core anti-double-booking invariant.

nodes.label: erd.drawio (8-entity ERD)
nodes.rationale: Drawn directly from the live Flyway schema (V1__init_schema.sql) so it matches what is actually running rather than the prose.

nodes.label: Tool: Spring Boot 4.1.0 / Spring Security / Data JPA
Tool: Next.js 16 / React 19 / TypeScript / Tailwind v4
R1 - Google Meet vs Calendly-style meeting links
nodes.rationale: Resolved that a free personal Gmail CAN generate Meet links via the Calendar API under user-OAuth2; the 'Workspace required' limit applies only to the Admin SDK / service-account domain-wide-delegation path. Custom booking UI is preserved because Meet only returns a link string. Pulled early because it affects the schema, though implemented last (M6).

nodes.label: R2 - Admin/provider dashboard patterns
nodes.rationale: Best practice found: calendar view with month/week/day toggle for overview plus a list/table view for detail, appointment cards showing service/consumer/time/status, colour-coding and multi-filter support; keep it simple and avoid clutter.

nodes.label: R3 - Landing-page sections + Claude Design prompts
nodes.rationale: Social-proof section deliberately dropped from the internal blueprint baseline because an MVP has no testimonials to show.

nodes.label: R4 - Calendar UX: popup vs dedicated page
nodes.rationale: Rule of thumb: flows with more than 3-4 steps or multi-field interaction belong on a dedicated page, not a modal; modals get clunky on mobile and are neither shareable nor crawlable.

nodes.label: Decision: per-provider Google connection from the start
nodes.rationale: Each provider does a one-time OAuth2 consent (calendar.events); the event is created on THEIR calendar with attendees=[consumer,provider] and sendUpdates=all, so the provider is the real host who can admit any edge-case knock, and the invited consumer joins directly with no waiting room.

nodes.label: Rejected: single operator host-account model
nodes.rationale: Rejected because one operator calendar would own every meeting across all providers, the absent operator (not the attending provider) would be the organizer and the only person able to clear a waiting-room knock, plus poor data separation.

nodes.label: Google Calendar API events.insert + conferenceData.createRequest
nodes.rationale: conferenceDataVersion=1 with a unique requestId and conferenceSolutionKey.type=hangoutsMeet returns the meeting URL as hangoutLink / conferenceData.entryPoints.

nodes.label: Meet admittance: guests on the event list are 'Trusted'
nodes.rationale: Anyone whose email is on the event's guest list joins directly with no host present and no manual admit while the waiting room is off; uninvited emails must knock - therefore both provider and consumer must be added as attendees on every booking.

nodes.label: OAuth verification vs test-user mode
nodes.rationale: Sensitive Calendar scopes require Google OAuth verification for a public production app, but test-user mode is sufficient for the bootcamp demo.

nodes.label: Calendly meeting-link pattern (comparison)
nodes.rationale: Calendly OAuth-connects the user's Google Calendar and sets Meet as the event location so Google generates the link; disable Calendar's automatic Meet setting to avoid two links.

nodes.label: Decision: one shared dashboard for PROVIDER and ADMIN
nodes.rationale: Same UI for both roles with the admin-only addition of a provider selector/filter; providers see only their own data. MVP pages kept to dashboard + services management + bulk-availability generator.

nodes.label: Landing section set (Hero -> How-it-works -> Services -> FAQ -> Footer)
nodes.rationale: MVP-appropriate section list with no social proof; the How-it-works section mirrors the documented user-journey text.

nodes.label: Decision: dedicated /book/[serviceId] page (not a modal)
nodes.rationale: The flow is multi-step (date -> provider dropdowns -> slot -> confirm) and needs a real URL as a clean auth-redirect-back target.

nodes.label: Provider gating + pasted fallback Meet link
nodes.rationale: A provider is not bookable until Google is connected; the fallback lets them paste a persistent personal Meet link so skipping OAuth does not block the product.

AuthController (register / login / me)
nodes.rationale: RegisterRequest has no role field at all, so a body-crafted role can never escalate a self-registration (FR-16).

nodes.label: AvailabilityManagementService (bulk generate/preview/delete)
nodes.rationale: Generation stays non-destructive: existing and booked slots are skipped, never overwritten - a flagged deviation from the design's 'replace' copy, and it makes re-running the generator idempotent.

nodes.label: ServiceController (public reads + admin CRUD + provider assignment)
GoogleCalendarService.createMeetingEvent
nodes.rationale: Never throws - a Meet-generation failure degrades to a booking without a link rather than failing the booking (NFR-4).

nodes.label: EmailService (consumer confirmation + provider notification)
nodes.rationale: Logs and swallows failures so a mail problem can never break an otherwise successful booking (NFR-4).

nodes.label: BookingStatus enum {CONFIRMED, CANCELLED, COMPLETED, NO_SHOW, VACANT}
LoadingOverlay (full-page blur during booking round-trip)
nodes.rationale: Covers the real latency of the synchronous Google Calendar + email round-trip so a slow booking does not read as broken.

nodes.label: CalendarDayCell (DS component, extended with total prop)
nodes.rationale: Extended with an optional `total` prop - a deliberate backward-compatible design-system extension rather than a fork of the component.

nodes.label: Accordion (DS component, provider slot lists + FAQ)
/appointments (consumer-only My Appointments)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately consumer-only after user pushback: providers/admins see their own consumer-side bookings via the '(You)' merge into /dashboard instead of a second page.

nodes.label: Demo seed migrations V3-V6 (services, providers/slots, admin, fallback links)
nodes.rationale: Demo data only, per the bootcamp rule; the admin seed was a bootstrapping requirement since only an admin can create or promote users and none existed yet.

nodes.label: Feature-based backend packaging (entity->repo->service->controller)
nodes.rationale: Packages by feature under com.ammar.bookingsystem with DTOs at the boundary and manual mapping - no MapStruct for the MVP.

nodes.label: Stateless JWT Bearer auth decision
nodes.rationale: Stateless session policy with the token in the Authorization header rather than a cookie, which is also why CORS needs no credentials support.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Spring Boot 4 needs spring-boot-starter-flyway
nodes.rationale: Boot 4 moved FlywayAutoConfiguration into its own module, so bare flyway-core never triggers it - Flyway silently never ran and the DB stayed empty with zero errors until ddl-auto: validate surfaced missing tables.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Jackson 3 relocation (tools.jackson.*)
nodes.rationale: com.fasterxml.jackson ObjectMapper compiles but throws NoClassDefFoundError at runtime on this stack; fixed by not depending on Jackson at all in the hand-rolled 401/403 JSON writer.

nodes.label: Gotcha: jjwt 0.13 API drift (parserBuilder no longer exists)
nodes.rationale: Even context7's own snippet showed the removed Jwts.parserBuilder(); corrected to Jwts.parser()...parseSignedClaims().

nodes.label: Bug: permitAll(/api/auth/**) also exposed /api/auth/me
nodes.rationale: Anonymous requests reached the controller and surfaced as an opaque 500 instead of a clean 401; fixed by naming /register and /login explicitly, and by adding logging to the blanket Exception handler so this class of bug cannot hide silently.

nodes.label: Bug: @PreAuthorize denials returned 500 instead of 403
nodes.rationale: Method-security AccessDeniedException is thrown inside the MVC handler invocation, so it never reaches SecurityConfig's filter-level accessDeniedHandler; needs its own @ExceptionHandler.

nodes.label: Bug: stale inverse @ManyToMany collection from first-level cache
nodes.rationale: Re-fetching the inverse side in the same persistence context returns the already-loaded instance with a stale lazy collection; fixed by building the response from the known new set instead of re-querying.

nodes.label: Bug: native number/date/time inputs render OS-locale digits
nodes.rationale: Chromium showed Arabic-Indic digits and Arabic month labels on an Arabic OS locale; converted to type=text with format placeholders and regex validation because this project has explicit RTL/Arabic i18n plans.

nodes.label: Bug: void @DeleteMapping returns 200 + empty body, not 204
nodes.rationale: The frontend api() helper only special-cased 204 before res.json(), so a successful delete surfaced as a UI error; fixed on both ends - explicit noContent() and a text check before parsing regardless of status.

nodes.label: Bug: DS Accordion used hooks without "use client"
nodes.rationale: Threw 'useState is not a function' at build time when rendered from the landing page's Server Component tree; fixed at the component itself since it is inherently interactive.

nodes.label: Bug: OAuth callback required code/state params
nodes.rationale: Google's most common non-happy-path - the provider clicking Cancel - redirects with error=access_denied and no code param at all, which threw an uncaught MissingServletRequestParameterException as a raw 500 page.

nodes.label: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE slot lock in booking transaction
nodes.rationale: Locks the slot row before validating AVAILABLE + horizon + provider-offers-service, so two concurrent bookings of the same slot cannot both succeed (second gets 409).

nodes.label: Signed 10-minute OAuth state JWT
nodes.rationale: Google's callback is a plain browser redirect carrying no Authorization header, so the initiating provider's id must travel in a short-lived purpose-tagged signed token.

nodes.label: Provider cannot book their own availability
nodes.rationale: Blocked server-side in BookingService before touching the DB (400) as well as filtered client-side, because the client filter alone is not trusted; providers may still book OTHER providers' services as consumers.

nodes.label: VACANT is a synthesized, never-persisted status
nodes.rationale: A dashboard-only label for open slots with a negative synthetic id; the V7 DB CHECK constraint deliberately excludes it so it can never be written even though it is a Java enum value.

nodes.label: '(You)' merge of own consumer-side bookings into /dashboard
nodes.rationale: Mixing a provider's own bookings-as-consumer into their dashboard is what makes a '(You)' marker meaningful - on /appointments every row is already self, so it would be redundant there.

nodes.label: Testing strategy (slice tests + curl + chrome-devtools walkthroughs)
nodes.rationale: A few focused @SpringBootTest/slice tests for the security guard, booking transaction and window validation; everything else verified manually via REST client and browser walkthroughs.
